extracted.intended_audience: General public, students, researchers, and policy practitioners interested in the Office of Management and Budget and U.S. federal budget/regulatory processes
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic overview of the Office of Management and Budget's responsibilities, processes, and the formal guidance (circulars, memoranda, committees) it issues to federal agencies. Useful for understanding how the executive branch coordinates budgets, reviews regulations, and enforces administrative requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with the president's budget and administration policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that agency reports, rules, testimony, and proposed legislation are consistent with the president's budget and administration policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB evaluates the effectiveness of agency programs, assesses competing funding demands among agencies, and sets funding priorities; it ensures agency outputs align with the president's budget and administration policies as part of its supervisory role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve administrative management and reduce public burdens
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve administrative management, develop better performance measures and coordinating mechanisms, and reduce unnecessary burdens on the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In overseeing procurement, financial management, information, and regulatory policies, OMB's role is to help agencies improve management practices and reduce unnecessary administrative burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget development and execution process (steps and deadlines)
rubrics_metrics.description: The multi-step, year-long process by which OMB coordinates the president's budget: inform the president of economic situation; issue Spring Guidance; issue Circular A-11 in July; agencies submit proposals by September; OMB meets with agencies; director meets president; agencies may appeal decisions in December; prepare budget justifications; president submits final budget by the first Monday in February.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The budget development/execution process is the primary device by which a president implements policies across the executive branch; OMB issues guidance and negotiates with agencies at each stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance and use of OMB circulars
rubrics_metrics.description: Circulars are instructions or information the OMB issues to federal agencies and are indexed by major category (e.g., Budget; State and Local Governments; Educational and Non-Profit Institutions; Federal Procurement; Federal Financial Management; Federal Information Resources / Data Collection; Other Special Purpose).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circulars provide formal, government-wide guidance and procedural requirements for agencies in their respective subject areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circular A-11 instructions for budget submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Circular A-11 outlines instructions for submitting budget proposals and due dates to all agencies (issued in July; agencies submit by September).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A-11 is a central OMB instruction used in the executive-branch budget development process and shapes agency submissions that become part of the president's budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circular A-119: adoption of voluntary consensus and international standards
rubrics_metrics.description: A-119 instructs agencies to adopt voluntary consensus standards and to minimize reliance on government-unique standards, supporting adoption of international standards where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adoption of international/voluntary consensus standards is widely followed by U.S. agencies (examples cited: EPA referencing ISO 14001; DOE referencing ISO 50001; FDA referencing ISO 13485 and ISO 22000). A-119 guides agencies on standard-selection priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program examiner duties and dual management-budget responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Program examiners are assigned to Resource Management Offices; they have dual responsibility for both management and budgetary issues, monitor agencies or topical areas, and act as expert advisers on program aspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Their tasks include reviewing agency budget requests, deciding which resource requests go to Congress, performing in-depth program evaluations (using tools such as the Program Assessment Rating Tool), reviewing proposed regulations and testimony, analyzing pending legislation, and overseeing aspects of the president's management agenda including agency management scorecards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the Program Assessment Rating Tool (PAR) for in-depth program evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Program examiners perform in-depth program evaluations using the Program Assessment Rating Tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAR is an OMB evaluation method used to assess program performance and inform budget/resource decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative Reference Division procedures for administration consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribute proposed legislation and testimony to all relevant federal reviewers and distill the comments into a consensus opinion of the administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Division writes Enrolled Bill Memoranda that detail a bill's particulars, opinions from relevant federal departments, and an overall recommendation about whether the president should sign or veto; it also issues Statements of Administration Policy to communicate the White House's position to Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of Statements of Administrative Policy (SAPs)
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB prepares SAPs with the president to communicate the president's and agencies' policies to the government as a whole and to set forth policymakers' agendas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SAPs are produced during budget review and are a formal mechanism for conveying administration positions to executive agencies and Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Review Division's technical coordination role
rubrics_metrics.description: The Budget Review Division performs government-wide budget coordination and handles the technical aspects related to the release of the president's budget each February.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For estimating executive-branch spending, BRD serves a purpose parallel to the Congressional Budget Office for Congressional spending, and parallels the Department of the Treasury for estimating executive-branch revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency Suspension and Debarment Committee (ISDC) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive departments and agencies must participate in a government-wide suspension and debarment system, issue regulations with government-wide criteria and minimum due process when debarring or suspending participants, and send debarred/suspended participants' identifying information to the General Services Administration for inclusion in the System for Award Management (SAM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ISDC was created by Executive Order 12549 (1986) and provides the government-wide framework and procedural requirements for suspension and debarment actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB coordination of agency procurement, financial management, information, and regulatory policies
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB oversees and coordinates administration-wide procurement, financial management, information, and regulatory policies to improve management and reduce burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Through offices such as OIRA, OFPP, OFFM, and OEGOV & IT, OMB provides subject-matter oversight and issues policies/circulars impacting agency operations in these domains.
